clinician.final_diagnosis: c-ANCA positive IBD with prominent extraintestinal manifestations
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old African-American man with no significant past medical history presented with a distinctive temporal sequence of organ involvement over 9 months. Initial extraintestinal manifestations included: (1) right eye anterior uveitis 7 months prior to admission, resolved with topical steroids; (2) right ear auricular chondritis 5 months prior, resolved spontaneously; (3) right wrist pain and redness diagnosed as cellulitis 2 months prior, with minimal improvement on antibiotics. Three days after wrist symptom onset, he was admitted with sudden fever and diarrhea (suspected viral etiology at presentation). Eight weeks after the wrist manifestations, he developed hematochezia, left lower quadrant pain, and perirectal abscess with fistula. Laboratory evaluation revealed markedly elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 11.1 mg/dL, ESR 124 mm/hour) and c-ANCA positivity at 1:40 titer with elevated anti-PR3 (102.6 units); p-ANCA and anti-MPO were negative. Colonoscopy with biopsies from the descending colon and rectum showed cryptitis, crypt abscesses, early crypt distortion, and basal plasmacytosis consistent with chronic colitis/IBD, without granulomas or vasculitis. Treatment was initiated with azathioprine and infliximab, resulting in fistula healing and sustained clinical improvement over 1.5 years with no further GI or extraintestinal manifestations.
